Distributor Declaration - Ethical Practices & Compliance

I/We {{ company_name }} hereby declare that I/We have undergone and understood following training and as a distributor of Meril, I/We am/are duty bound to follow various procedural frameworks developed and adopted by the Management from time to time. I/We have been explained various Code of Conduct which shall be followed by me as a Distributor for ethical conduct of Meril's business. I/We have read and understood following Code of Conduct in consensus-ad-idem :

[ 1 ] Anti Bribery and Anti Corruption Policy
[ 2 ] Export Controls and Trade Sanctions Policy
[ 3 ] HCP & HCO Compliance framework
[ 4 ] National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority norms for capping of maximum retail price & maximum trade margin across all trade channels
[ 5 ] FCPA (Foreign Corrupt Practices Act)
[ 6 ] UCMPMD (Uniform Code for Marketing Practices in Medical Devices)

MERIL DISTRIBUTOR COMPLIANCE POLICY

Healthcare professionals (HCP) and Healthcare Organizations (HCO) can be engaged for the below scientific activities

1.0   Sponsorship to 3rd party congress/conference/Meetings:

Sponsorship supports to 3rd party congress/conferences/Meetings are intended to share and spread advancement and technology among medical fraternity. It also gives the Sponsor an opportunity to showcase its products and advancement in technology. Following are important points to be kept in mind while extending Sponsorship support:

  • Sponsorship support to be provided only for scientific and educational program/ conference/ congresses.
  • The scientific content/topics at a conference should be aligned to the products or therapies in which Meril is dealing.
  • Sponsorship amount should be modest and at par with the offerings to other sponsors.
  • In lieu of the sponsorship amount, entitlement such as Stall, Training village, Scientific Session should be provided.
  • Proper accounting along with required supporting documents should be maintained for record.
  • The following points shall be kept in mind while providing sponsorship support
  • Sponsorship amount can only be provided to Health Care Organization (HCO).
  • Sponsorship amount shall not be given as a reward or inducement for usage of Meril's products or services ;
  • Sponsorship amount shall not be given for the purpose of Off-label Promotion of a Product;
  • Sponsorship amount shall not be given in exchange of influencing regulatory, pricing, formulary or reimbursement decisions

2.0   Training and Education:

Training and education programs are Meril initiated programs, focused in the safe and effective use of Meril's products. Such Training and Education Programs can include hands on sessions, lectures and presentations on topics related to Meril's products or therapies. Following are important points to be kept in mind while extending support for Training and Educational programs:

  • Content/topics of Training and Education (T & E) program should be aligned to Meril's products or therapies.
  • Expenses for such T&E program should be recorded in books with necessary supporting documents.
  • Venue should be conducive to conduct training and educational programs,
  • Reasonable travel and modest lodging can be arranged for attending HCPs.
  • Limits for HCP accommodation are as per the following :
    Metro CitiesNon-Metro CitiesInternational Stay
    INR 8,000/-
    (exclusive of taxes)    		INR 6000/- (exclusive of taxes)USD 300
    (exclusive of taxes)
    Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Ahmadabad, Pune, Visakhapatnam, Surat, Jaipur, NagpurAll other Cities not included in list of Metro Cities will be considered as Non-Metro Cities
  • Hospitality to HCPs should be in the form of meal arrangements only and should be modest in nature. Limits for HCP hospitality expenses should be as per the following :
    BreakfastLunchSnacksDinner
    INR 1000/-INR 2500/-INR 1000/-INR 2500/-
    NOTE : Alcoholic Drink is permitted only during dinner and it has to be incidental to dinner
  • Arranging meals, travel, or other expenses for guests of HCPs or any other person not having bona fide professional interest in the information shared during program is strictly not allowed.
  • Training and education programs should not be organized to secure an improper advantage or to please HCPs.

3.0   Grant (Monetary/Non-Monetary):

Grant (Monetary/Non-Monetary) can be provided to Health Care Organizations (hereinafter "HCO") including and not limited to, a hospital, university, medical associations, institute or organization) for Scientific, Educational, Charity and better patient outcome purpose.

  • Grant should be provided for the purpose of supporting Scientific, Educational and Charitable activities which in turn brings better healthcare outcome and benefits to the patients.
  • Grant support has to be properly documented and recorded in books with necessary supporting documents.
  • Grant can only be provided to Healthcare Organization (HCO)
  • Grant amount shall not be given as a reward or inducement for usage of Meril's products or services ;
  • Grant amount shall not be given for the purpose of Off-label Promotion of a Product;
  • Grant amount shall not be given for influencing regulatory, pricing, formulary or reimbursement decisions.

4.0   Awareness Program:

Therapy Awareness programs are designed to increase awareness amongst general public with respect to underlying clinical conditions and innovation in medical field with treatment options and therapies.

  • Therapy Awareness Programs should be conducted in collaboration with HCP experienced in relevant therapy.
  • Awareness Programs can be designed in the form of Awareness Camps for Patients, Article Publications in newspapers and Magazines, Radio Activity.
  • Awareness program should not lead to any publicity/promotion/profiling to any HCP or HCO. Ensure to follow THE NATIONAL MEDICAL COMMISSION ACT, 2019. Only HCP name, Designation, Associated Hospital name and small size photo can be included where awareness article contents are provided by HCP In case of Article Publications in Newspapers and Magazines.
  • Product promotion to general public is not allowed subject to provision of The DRUGS AND MAGIC REMEDIES ACT, 1954.
  • The DRUGS AND MAGIC REMEDIES ACT, 1954 prohibit any false or misleading advertisement.
  • Expenses for such programs should be recorded in books with required supporting documents

5.0   HCP Services:

Engaging HCPs to provide valuable bona fide services such as a speaker, proctor, trainer, advisor, etc. During scientific, training or education program on effective use of Meril products and therapy. Following points to be kept in mind while considering HCP's engagement:

  • Identify and document legitimate business need and purpose for HCP service.
  • Selection of HCP should be on the basis of the HCPs qualifications and expertise in relevant field to address the identified purpose and should not be on the basis of past or potential purchases.
  • HCP agreement must be in writing, clearly defining scope of work and services to be performed and compensation to be provided. HCP service agreement has to be signed off by all the parties prior to the commencement of services post internal approval.
  • Compensation/service fees paid to HCPs must be consistent with the fair market value.
  • HCP service fees/compensation shall not be paid without valid agreement and HCP work completion report.

For all the above mentioned activities kindly reach out to Meril Business Manager.

Compliance Code of Conduct for Meril Distributors

1.   INTRODUCTION

Meril aim is to improve the quality of human life through innovative and advanced healthcare solutions. To achieve this, we continually work towards innovation in manufacturing medical technology. Meril collaborates with physicians to identify unmet clinical needs, develop revolutionary therapies and work towards bringing new advancement in its products. It is also important that such advancement in medical field should reach to larger group and more patients get benefit of available therapies and add More to Life. In the course of such interaction, Meril is committed to the highest standards of integrity, and adheres to the spirit of all laws and regulations of the countries in which it operates whether such business is carried out through direct sales operations or through Distributors. To enable this goal, it is important to adhere to ethical and legal standards in our interaction with Health Care Professionals/Health Care Organizations. In view of the same, a definitive Compliance Code of Conduct by Meril Distributors have been defined and presented to the Distributor for due compliance of the same.

Meril {{ meril_company_names }} is hereinafter referred to as "Meril".
{{ company_name }} is hereinafter referred to as "Distributor".
It is warranted from the Distributors to observe and adhere to this Code of Conduct. Failure to comply may result in termination of the commercial relationship with Meril and Distributor will be responsible for any other legal implication.

2.   APPLICABILITY

This policy is applicable to any person or legal entity who is and/or proposed to be, engaged and/or working for or on behalf of Meril for sale, marketing, promotion, or distribution of Meril's products, including but not limited to dealers, agents, resellers, distributors, business partners, consultants, contractors, marketing support, brokers or advisors who buy and resell Meril's products and/or earn a commission on the sale of Meril's products.

3.   COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS

Meril is committed to comply with Indian laws and laws of other countries that are, or may be, of potential relevance, including but not limited to laws applicable to bribery, and/or corrupt payments, including, National Medical Commission Act (NMC), Uniform Code of Pharmaceuticals and Marketing Practices (UCPMP), Drugs and Magical Remedies Act, National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), Goods and Service Tax, Income Tax, Prevention of Corruption Act (PoCA), all applicable national, regional, provincial, state, municipal or local laws and regulations that prohibit tax evasion, or otherwise dealing in the bribery of, or the providing of, facilitation payments, or other benefits to, any government official or any other person. This Compliance Code of Conduct is applicable to all the individuals, distributors, agents, channel partners, acting on behalf of Meril.

4.   BOOKS AND RECORDS

Distributor shall keep complete, genuine, accurate and timely records of all expenses and transactions pertaining to sales and marketing of Meril products or services. All such transactions must be recorded with reasonable details along with supporting documents in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

5.   CONFLICTS OF INTEREST

Distributor shall avoid actual or apparent conflicts of interest and should make sound Business decisions in the best interests of Meril, undistorted by personal interests. A conflict of interest may exist whenever a Distributor's private interests or personal Activities or relationships interfere or appear to interfere with the duties warranted towards Meril. If you discover that a personal activity, investment, interest or Association compromises – or even appear to compromise – your objectivity or ability to make impartial business decisions, disclose it immediately to your designated Meril sales representative and Business Head, who will contact the Meril Compliance Head to obtain approval, if appropriate.

6.   TRAINING AND EDUCATION OF HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS

Training and Education programs are important for safe and effective use of Meril products. Programs can include hands on sessions, lectures, presentations on topics related to Meril product or therapies. If there is a need for a Distributor to conduct such training and education program, a separate written communication to be made to Meril and follow the process suggested for the same.

7.   GIFTS, TRAVELS, OR ENTERTAINMENT

Gifts, travel and entertainment offerings that give the appearance of improper business advantage are strictly prohibited. If there is a need for Distributors to extend any reasonable support, a separate written communication to be made to Meril and follow the process suggested for the same. Such gifts, travel, and entertainment should be permitted under applicable laws, modest in value, infrequent, reasonable and for a legitimate purpose.

8.   EDUCATIONAL GRANTS

Educational Grants are permitted only if the grant is intended for Scientific, Educational, Charity and better patient outcome purposes. Such Grants should be independent and not linked with the volume or value of purchases made by, or anticipated from, the grant recipients. If there is a need for Distributors to provide the same, a separate written communication to be made to Meril and follow the process suggested for the same.

9.   DISCOUNTS/REBATES & COMMISSION

Discounts/Rebates and Commission must be defined and approved before the time of sale in form of written contract between the parties and must not result in personal benefit to any HCP/HCO or government official.

10.   COMPLIANCE WITH POLICY AND TERMINATION ON NON-COMPLIANCE

It is the responsibility of the Distributor to ensure that their Representatives understand and comply with Meril Distributor's Compliance Code of Conduct Policy, and the Distributor shall self-monitor their adherence to this Code of Conduct. The Distributor understand and acknowledges that if it is determined or believed that at any time a Distributor or its Representatives have failed to comply with the standards set forth in this Code of Conduct, then Meril shall have all right to determine the relationship without notice and without any liability or obligation of any nature whatsoever.

***SELF – DECLARATION CERTIFICATION OF COMPLIANCE***

I have read and understood Meril Distributor Compliance Code of Conduct and hereby declare that I will adhere in all respects to the ethics and standards of conducts described in it. I further confirm my understanding that any non-adherence may be subject to appropriate disciplinary action, which may include termination of the commercial relationship with Meril. This policy supplements, but does not supersede, any and all rights maintained by Meril under any contract with the Distributor.
